fixes.explanation: Yes. Paul says, "Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast." He just called it fool talk, and I think he'd rather not. It's like a coworker bragging all week until you finally have to speak up.
That's him. Paul says, "Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I." Abraham is the man God made promises to (Genesis 12:2–3). Paul has the family papers, and he isn't afraid to pull them out.

Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a great name, but it's not the one in this verse. Paul says, "Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I." The name in the text is Abraham. Moses never shows up in these verses.

That's right. Paul says, "…three times I was shipwrecked." Three! I'd have taken one look at a boat after the first one and started walking everywhere. And Paul is telling the Corinthians all of this himself.

The text says it right out. Paul lists "…danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles…" so the danger came from his own people and from the non-Jews. That's a heavy thing to say about your own countrymen. Paul says it plainly.

Yes. Paul says, "The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying." He calls on God Himself as the one who knows. When you've just listed all that, you might want somebody to turn to who knows the whole story. And God is the one Paul names.
